# SEC TRIBUNAL — PROSECUTION'S BEAR CASE
## In re: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA)

Your Honors, the evidence in Exhibit A tells a story of a company whose growth engine has stalled, whose profitability has been cut to a fraction of its peak, and whose balance sheet is quietly re-leveraging. The prosecution presents the following charges.

---

**CHARGE 1: Revenue growth has collapsed into outright decline.**

Tesla grew revenue 51.4% in FY2022, then 18.8% in FY2023 — and then the engine seized. FY2024 revenue grew a mere 0.9% ($96.77B → $97.69B), and FY2025 revenue *fell* 2.9% to $94.83B [Exhibit A]. A company priced for growth delivered negative growth. The FY2025 top line ($94.83B) sits below FY2023's ($96.77B) — two full years of stagnation-turned-contraction.

**CHARGE 2: Operating income has been cut by more than two-thirds from its peak.**

Operating income peaked at $13.66B in FY2022. It then fell relentlessly: $8.89B (FY2023), $7.08B (FY2024), and $4.36B (FY2025) — a 68% collapse in three years [Exhibit A]. Operating margin cratered from 16.8% (FY2022) to 4.6% (FY2025). Most damning: the most recent quarter, Q2 FY2026, posted operating income of just $398.0M — a 1.4% operating margin, and *below* the $923.0M earned in the year-ago quarter (2025-06-30) despite 25.5% revenue growth [Exhibit A]. Revenue up, operating profit down 57% — the incremental business is being sold at deeply inferior economics.

**CHARGE 3: Gross margins have structurally deteriorated and remain volatile.**

Gross margin stood at 25.6% in FY2022. It has since been stuck in the high teens: 18.2% (FY2023), 17.9% (FY2024), 18.0% (FY2025) [Exhibit A]. Absolute gross profit shrank three consecutive years — $20.85B (FY2022) → $17.66B → $17.45B → $17.09B (FY2025) — even as revenue rose $13B over that span. The quarterly record shows no durable recovery: 16.3% (Q1 2025), a brief 21.1% (Q1 2026), then straight back down to 16.8% (Q2 2026) [Exhibit A].

**CHARGE 4: Net income has collapsed 75% from peak, with the bottom line thinning quarter after quarter.**

Net income fell from $15.00B (FY2023) to $7.09B (FY2024) to $3.79B (FY2025) — a 75% decline in two years [Exhibit A]. Net margin compressed from 15.5% to 4.0%. Quarterly, Q1 FY2026 net income was $477.0M (2.1% net margin), and Q2 FY2026 was $1.11B — *below* the year-ago Q2 2025 figure of $1.17B despite the higher revenue [Exhibit A]. Earnings power is eroding on both an annual and year-over-year quarterly basis.

**CHARGE 5: Debt and liabilities are climbing steadily while cash drifts lower.**

Long-term debt has risen nearly 8-fold from its FY2022 trough of $1.03B to $7.72B at Q2 FY2026 (2026-06-30), rising every single quarter on record: $4.99B → $5.61B → $6.58B → $7.64B → $7.72B [Exhibit A]. Total liabilities have more than doubled from $28.42B (FY2020) to $61.01B (Q2 FY2026), including a $10.5B increase in just four quarters (from $50.49B at 2025-06-30) [Exhibit A]. Meanwhile, cash & equivalents *fell* to $15.22B at 2026-06-30 — below the $16.25B held back in FY2022. Borrowing more while cash declines and earnings shrink is the classic anatomy of a weakening credit story.

**CHARGE 6: Soaring R&D spend is producing no return in the P&L.**

R&D expense has nearly tripled from $2.59B (FY2021) to $6.41B (FY2025), and the quarterly run-rate keeps accelerating — $1.41B (Q1 2025) to $2.37B (Q2 2026), a 68% jump in five quarters [Exhibit A]. Yet over the same period operating income fell from $6.52B (FY2021) to $4.36B (FY2025), and the latest quarter's operating income ($398.0M) is now *one-sixth* of the same quarter's R&D bill ($2.37B) [Exhibit A]. The company is spending ever more on the future while the present business decays beneath it.

---

**SUMMARY:** Revenue shrinking (FY2025: -2.9%). Operating margin down from 16.8% to 4.6% annually, and 1.4% in the latest quarter. Net income down 75% from peak. Long-term debt up 7.5x from its trough and rising every quarter. Cash lower than three years ago. The prosecution submits that Exhibit A depicts a company in structural profit decline financing its ambitions with a deteriorating core. The prosecution rests.

# DEFENSE REBUTTAL — In re: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA)

Your Honors, the prosecution has presented a snapshot framed at maximum darkness. The Defense will show that the headwinds cited are sector-wide, the spending is deliberate, the balance sheet is among the strongest in the industry, and the most recent data show a reacceleration the prosecution declined to mention. We answer each charge in turn, using the prosecution's own exhibits.

---

## CHARGE 1 — "Revenue growth has collapsed into outright decline." **REBUTTED.**

**Industry context:** FY2025 was a down year for the entire sector. Tesla's revenue fell 2.9%; General Motors' revenue fell 2.1% in the same fiscal year ($171.61B → $167.97B) [Exhibit B]. This is a shared macro headwind, not a Tesla-specific failure.

**Improving recent trend — the prosecution's fatal omission:** The most recent quarters show growth has decisively resumed:

- Q1 FY2026: revenue **+15.8% YoY** ($19.34B → $22.39B) [Exhibit A]
- Q2 FY2026: revenue **+25.5% YoY** ($22.50B → $28.24B) [Exhibit A]

Compare the peer: GM's Q1 FY2026 revenue *declined* 1.3% and Q2 grew just 2.1% [Exhibit B]. My client is growing revenue at more than **ten times** the rate of its direct competitor in the latest reported quarter. The "seized engine" is running again — the prosecution simply stopped reading the tape at FY2025.

---

## CHARGE 2 — "Operating income cut by two-thirds." **CONTEXT AND ARITHMETIC REBUT THE CHARGE.**

**Industry context:** GM's operating income collapsed from $12.78B (FY2024) to **$2.91B (FY2025) — a 77% single-year decline**, worse than anything alleged against my client [Exhibit B]. GM's FY2025 operating margin was **1.7%** versus Tesla's **4.6%** [Exhibits A, B]. If a 4.6% margin is an indictable offense, the entire industry stands accused — and my client stands accused less than its peer.

**The Q2 FY2026 quarter, explained by arithmetic:** The prosecution's most damning exhibit — operating income falling from $923.0M to $398.0M YoY — is almost entirely a spending decision, not a business decay. In that same year, quarterly R&D rose from $1.59B to $2.37B, an increase of $780M [Exhibit A]. The operating income decline was $525M. **The deliberate R&D increase more than accounts for the entire shortfall.** Absent the stepped-up investment, operating income would have *grown* alongside the 25.5% revenue growth.

---

## CHARGE 3 — "Gross margins structurally deteriorated." **PARTIALLY CONCEDED; TREND REBUTTED.**

The Defense concedes candidly: the FY2022 gross margin of 25.6% has not returned, and 18% is the new baseline [Exhibit A]. We will not spin that.

But the prosecution overstates decay and understates recovery:

1. **Stabilization, not deterioration:** 18.2% → 17.9% → 18.0% across FY2023–FY2025 is a floor, not a slide [Exhibit A].
2. **Gross profit dollars are now growing again:** Q1 FY2026 gross profit was $4.72B versus $3.15B a year prior — **+50% YoY**. Q2 FY2026 was $4.75B versus $3.88B — **+22% YoY** [Exhibit A].
3. **Peer comparison:** GM does not report gross profit under standard tags [Exhibit B], but its operating margin never exceeded 8.2% in any year on record and stood at 1.7% in FY2025 [Exhibit B]. Tesla's underlying unit economics remain superior to the industry incumbent even at the compressed margin level.

---

## CHARGE 4 — "Net income collapsed 75% from peak." **THE PEAK WAS INFLATED; THE COMPARISON IS UNFAIR.**

The prosecution anchors to FY2023's $15.00B net income. Note what the prosecution does not: FY2023 **operating** income was only $8.89B [Exhibit A]. Net income exceeded operating income by more than $6B, and net margin (15.5%) exceeded operating margin (9.2%) — a clear signature of large non-operating, non-recurring benefit in that year. Measuring decline from an artificially elevated one-off peak is prosecutorial framing, not analysis.

**Recent quarters and peer context:** Tesla's Q2 FY2026 net income of $1.11B was essentially flat versus the year-ago $1.17B — *while absorbing $780M of additional quarterly R&D* [Exhibit A]. Meanwhile GM's quarterly net margins ran 3.0% in Q3 2025 and 3.0% in Q2 FY2026 [Exhibit B] — comparable to Tesla's 3.9% in the same quarter [Exhibit A]. The bottom line is compressed sector-wide, and my client is not the laggard.

---

## CHARGE 5 — "Re-leveraging while cash drifts lower." **THIS CHARGE FAILS ON ITS OWN NUMBERS.**

This is the prosecution's weakest charge, and Exhibit B destroys it:

- **Leverage:** Tesla's LT-debt/equity is **0.09** [Exhibit A]. Its total liabilities of $61.01B are covered 1.4x by stockholders' equity of $86.86B. GM carries **$219.10B of liabilities against $62.00B of equity** — roughly 3.5x levered [Exhibit B]. Tesla is, by a wide margin, the *less* levered company in this courtroom.
- **The "8-fold" debt increase:** $1.03B to $7.72B [Exhibit A] is an increase from a near-zero base to a still-trivial figure. Cash of $15.22B covers long-term debt of $7.72B nearly **twice over**. Interest expense fell from $685M (FY2019) to $156M (FY2023) [Exhibit A].
- **Liabilities rose because the company grew:** Over the four quarters the prosecution cites, liabilities rose $10.5B — while total assets rose ~$20B ($128.57B → $148.52B) and equity rose every single quarter ($77.31B → $86.86B) [Exhibit A]. That is asset-building, not distress.
- **Cash generation:** Operating cash flow was $14.75B in FY2025, essentially flat with $14.92B in FY2024 despite the margin compression, and Q1 FY2026 OCF was **$3.94B, up 82%** from $2.16B a year earlier [Exhibit A]. A "weakening credit story" does not generate $14B+ of operating cash annually with debt covered twice by cash on hand.

---

## CHARGE 6 — "R&D producing no return." **THE RETURN IS ON THE TOP LINE; THE FUNDING IS INTERNAL.**

**Deliberate growth investment:** R&D rose from $2.59B (FY2021) to $6.41B (FY2025) [Exhibit A] — a choice, funded entirely from $14.75B of operating cash flow, not borrowed distress capital. And the return is already visible where returns first appear: **revenue reaccelerated to +15.8% and +25.5% YoY** in the two most recent quarters [Exhibit A], while gross profit grew +50% and +22% YoY in those same quarters.

rebuttal:
# PROSECUTION'S REBUTTAL — In re: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA)

Your Honors, the Defense has performed admirably with weak material. The prosecution will be brief, will note the concession on the record, and will dismantle the two points where the Defense's arithmetic simply does not survive contact with Exhibit A.

---

**FOR THE RECORD: The Defense concedes Charge 3.** Counsel stated plainly that "the FY2022 gross margin of 25.6% has not returned, and 18% is the new baseline." The concession is accepted. And the Defense's claimed "floor" cracked the moment they built it: the most recent quarter, Q2 FY2026, printed **16.8% gross margin** [Exhibit A] — below the conceded 18% baseline, below FY2023, FY2024, and FY2025. That is not stabilization. That is a floor giving way.

---

**REBUTTAL 1: The "R&D explains the shortfall" defense proves the prosecution's case on incremental economics.**

The Defense's cleverest move is arguing that Q2 FY2026's operating collapse ($923.0M → $398.0M) is "almost entirely" the $780M R&D step-up. Look at what this argument requires the court to ignore: revenue grew **$5.74B** year-over-year that quarter ($22.50B → $28.24B), yet gross profit grew only **$870M** ($3.88B → $4.75B) [Exhibit A]. That is a **15.2% incremental gross margin** — dramatically below even the compressed 17.2% of the prior year. The new revenue is *worse* business than the old revenue. The Defense cannot excuse the operating line with R&D while the gross line — which sits *above* R&D in the income statement — deteriorates on its own. The 25.5% revenue growth the Defense celebrates arrived at a 16.8% gross margin and a 1.4% operating margin. Growth purchased at those economics is not exoneration; it is the charge itself.

---

**REBUTTAL 2: "Revenue has reacceleratated" — measured against a collapsed base.**

The Defense trumpets +15.8% and +25.5% YoY growth in Q1 and Q2 FY2026. But examine the comparison quarters: Q1 2025 revenue of $19.34B and Q2 2025 of $22.50B were themselves the *trough quarters* of a year in which annual revenue **declined 2.9%** [Exhibit A]. Growing 25.5% off a depressed base is arithmetic, not recovery — and note that Q2 FY2026 revenue of $28.24B barely exceeds Q3 2025's $28.09B, achieved three quarters earlier. Meanwhile, the "reaccelerated" quarters delivered: net income of $477.0M (Q1, a **2.1% net margin**) and $1.11B (Q2, *below* the year-ago $1.17B) [Exhibit A]. A recovery that grows the top line 25% while shrinking the bottom line is a recovery in name only.

---

**REBUTTAL 3: The "inflated FY2023 peak" defense concedes more than it wins.**

The prosecution grants the Defense's point that FY2023's $15.00B net income contained non-operating benefit — the gap versus $8.89B of operating income supports it. Very well: strike FY2023 and use the Defense's preferred clean anchor. Operating income still reads $13.66B (FY2022) → $4.36B (FY2025), a **68% decline** requiring no one-time items to explain [Exhibit A]. Or use FY2024 net income of $7.09B → FY2025's $3.79B: a **47% decline in a single year** with no accounting asterisk available. The Defense has successfully argued that the collapse is smaller than 75%. It remains a collapse.

---

The prosecution does not contest the Defense on Charge 5. Cash of $15.22B against long-term debt of $7.72B, equity rising every quarter, and $14.75B of annual operating cash flow [Exhibit A] — the balance-sheet charge does not carry, and we withdraw emphasis from it rather than waste the tribunal's time.

But the core indictment stands untouched: the Defense's own showcase quarter — Q2 FY2026 — delivered a 16.8% gross margin, a 1.4% operating margin, and year-over-year declines in both operating and net income despite 25.5% revenue growth [Exhibit A]. The prosecution rests on the Defense's best evidence.

verdict.summary: The prosecution charged Tesla with collapsing revenue growth, a two-thirds decline in operating income, structural gross margin deterioration, a 75% net income collapse, re-leveraging, and unproductive R&D spending. The defense successfully rebutted the balance-sheet charge (which the prosecution withdrew) and demonstrated top-line reacceleration (+15.8% and +25.5% YoY in the two most recent quarters), but conceded gross margin deterioration and could not overcome the evidence that recent growth arrives at sharply inferior economics — a 16.8% gross margin, 1.4% operating margin, and year-over-year declines in operating and net income in the latest quarter. The tribunal finds a company with a fortress balance sheet and robust cash generation, but a genuinely and materially degraded profit engine.

verdict.recommendation: Tesla presents a bifurcated investment picture. The balance sheet is unambiguously strong — $15.22B in cash covering $7.72B of long-term debt nearly twice, equity rising every quarter, 0.09 debt-to-equity, and $14.75B of annual operating cash flow — so solvency risk is negligible. But the profit engine has genuinely degraded: operating margin fell from 16.8% to 4.6% annually and just 1.4% in the latest quarter, gross margins have settled near 17-18% with the most recent quarter at 16.8%, and — most concerning — the celebrated 25.5% revenue reacceleration arrived at a 15.2% incremental gross margin, meaning new revenue is lower-quality than old revenue. Investors should treat this as a well-capitalized company making a large, unproven R&D bet while its core economics compress. Suitable only for investors with high risk tolerance and a multi-year horizon who believe the elevated R&D will convert to margin recovery; the near-term earnings trajectory does not support a growth-stock premium, and any position should be sized accordingly with margin trends over the next several quarters as the key monitoring signal.
